newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE PROGRAMME.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the English premier league this weekend (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT):
Former Leicester manager Brian Little will be looking for three points against his former club in what is likely to be a closely-fought midlands derby.
Blackburn may be bottom but beat Liverpool 3-0 in their last match and could get at least a draw against big-spending Chelsea, who may give a debut to new Italian signing Gianfranco Zola.

Everton are likely to be without injured Duncan Ferguson again against a Southampton side improved by the recent signings of Norwegian Claus Lundekvam, Israeli Eyal Berkovic, Dutchman Ulrich Van Gobbel and Norwegian Egil Ostenstad. But the Saints could be without Matt LeTissier, who has an ankle injury.

Former Liverpool marksman Ian Rush, who may be playing on the right-wing, will be looking to score his first goal for Leeds against his previous team and end a 13-match scoreless run, the worst of his career. Evans awaits the result of fitness checks on Stig Bjornebye (ankle) and Dominic Matteo (ankle) before naming his team.

Manchester United will be looking to end a run of three straight defeats against a confident Arsenal side who are unbeaten in seven. United will be without suspended midfielder Roy Keane but Ryan Giggs is fit again and ready to start his first senior game since September 29.
Full-strength league leaders Newcastle should prove too strong for erratic West Ham in front of another capacity crowd at St James' Park where they beat the London side 3-0 last season.

Spurs, who could have Darren Anderton back for the first time since September 25, beat Sunderland 2-1 in the League Cup three weeks ago and will be looking to chalk up a fifth successive home win against manager Peter Reid's feisty but inconsistent battlers.

Wimbledon will be looking to stretch their uneaten run to 14 while Coventry, under new coach Gordon Strachan, will be hoping to pick themselves up after their shock League Cup defeat to second division Gillingham on Wednesday.

Middlesbrough's new-found confidence and prestige is under serious threat with reports that Brazilian Emerson wants to quit and compatriot Juninho wants to go. They desperately need to win after six league games without a victory.
Two teams who have forgotten how to win face each other at Hillsborough where Forest would dearly love a repeat of their 3-1 win there last season.
